target.title: fix(repair): preserve immutable retry inputs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where retry and self-heal dispatches could reconstruct repair jobs from mutable defaults or incomplete legacy artifacts, changing the original runner, mode, sandbox, model, or dry-run behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each repair attempt now records a bounded immutable input snapshot and retry paths recover the newest exact snapshot before considering durable or legacy fallback data. Recovery fails closed to plan-only, dry-run behavior when exact inputs are unavailable; historical final and worker artifact families remain supported without restoring the reverted action-lifecycle ledger or raw review-log machinery.

Self-heal recovery uses a shared three-minute scan deadline, so unavailable artifacts cannot consume the workflow's entire runtime budget.

## User Impact

Operators can requeue failed repair jobs without silently promoting permissions or changing the original execution inputs. Older runs remain recoverable through a narrow compatibility parser, while ambiguous or incomplete artifacts are rejected.

target.title: fix(repair): publish only validated target commits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repair validation could prove one checkout state and later publish a mutable
`HEAD`, while target-controlled Git state, ignored runtime inputs, setup hooks,
filesystem metadata, network access, or surviving descendants could influence
later credential-bearing publication.

## Current Design

- publishes only the immutable validated commit SHA through hook-free isolated
  Git with a branch lease sampled before validation
- runs target commands in delegated Linux user, mount, network, and PID
  namespaces; only the target checkout and disposable profile/runtime roots are
  writable
- makes the remaining filesystem recursively read-only, applies Landlock, then
  drops and verifies all inheritable, permitted, effective, bounding, and
  ambient capabilities before target execution
- enables loopback inside the isolated network namespace without exposing host
  listeners
- contains pnpm, Bun, and npm dependency installation, disables pnpmfile and
  package lifecycle hooks, and rejects unsafe npm script options
- recursively binds ignored runtime symlink targets, clears broader disposable
  build/cache roots between commands, and rejects residual gitlinks
- rejects redirected or symlinked Git object stores before authenticated Git
- uses isolated Git for every rebase continuation and publication transition,
  while preserving exact-SHA checkout binding and detached-process reaping

The configurable repair runner contract requires Linux, delegated user
namespaces, mount/network/PID namespaces, and Landlock ABI 3 or newer. Runners
without that boundary fail closed.

## Exact-Head Evidence

Head: `e65ec1565f62468248edfaec1d8991b51cce3636`

- GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29342344031
  - `pnpm check` passed in 7m52s: 2,029 tests, 2,021 passed, 8
    platform/environment skips, 0 failed
  - both TypeScript builds, lint, formatting, workflow semantics, unit/repair
    tests, and coverage gates passed
  - Windows Codex launcher and crawl-remote toolchain integration passed
- CodeQL: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29342344080
  - Actions and JavaScript/TypeScript analyses passed
- hosted Linux namespace proof: AWS Crabbox run `run_5375a120d369`, lease
  `cbx_609c7e0f5271`
  - exact working tree synced with both builds passing
  - metadata writes and read-only remount bypass were blocked after capability
    removal
  - isolated loopback communication passed while host-local listener access
    remained blocked
  - Bun and npm setup descendants were rejected and reaped
  - the immediate detached double-fork regression passed deterministically
  - 6 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; lease stopped automatically
- local focused builds, repair lint, formatting, and source-containment checks
  passed
- release-owned `CHANGELOG.md` remains untouched

## Findings Addressed

- trusted runner/ClawSweeper/PATH filesystem writes, including metadata
  operations not mediated by Landlock
- mutable external ignored-runtime symlink inputs
- pnpmfile setup hooks and uncontained Bun/npm installation
- host-network namespace access while preserving isolated localhost workflows
- legacy Git continuations and late lease sampling
- redirected Git object stores
- broader ignored runtime roots and residual gitlinks
- unsafe npm post-script options

## Commits In This Follow-Up

- `4a922c6fee` `fix(repair): isolate validation filesystem and network`
- `57f83a3c09` `fix(repair): bind validation runtime inputs`
- `78596b1051` `fix(repair): isolate Git transitions and publication`
- `e65ec1565f` `fix(repair): drop validation namespace capabilities`

includes the reverted lifecycle expansion.

target.title: fix(review): bind mutations to reviewed activity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClawSweeper could reuse a trusted pull-request verdict and continue apply or automerge mutations after a human added a review, inline comment, or review-thread resolution change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a bounded digest-only cursor over reviews, inline comments, and thread resolution state. Review reuse performs stable two-scan reads; trusted automerge and apply revalidate immediately before each mutation request; incomplete, unstable, or cursor-less legacy state fails closed for a fresh review. Cursor ordering is locale-independent.

This restores only review-activity freshness from the reverted lifecycle work. It does not restore raw review logs, broad workflow transactions, or the wider https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/521 architecture.

## User Impact

Maintainers can rely on new review activity stopping stale labels, repair/review dispatch, apply, and merge actions before the next GitHub mutation. Existing cursor-less verdicts pause until refreshed instead of being trusted silently.

target.title: fix(ledger): preserve interrupted attempt mutations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interrupted repair execution could lose the mutation boundary entirely: current production emitted no `workflow.attempt` lifecycle, dangling `repair.execute` starts stayed open after crashes, and an earlier unknown outcome could override a later observed result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds one narrow wrapper around the existing execute-fix command. It records bounded `workflow.attempt` and `repair.execute` start/outcome receipts, preserves the exact child exit or signal, terminalizes uncertain child receipts before the parent, folds outcomes by idempotency key and phase order, and publishes the finalized shards through the existing immutable state path. It does not restore the reverted PR 521 lifecycle or transaction modules.

## User Impact

Maintainers get production-backed interruption evidence for repair execution. Hard-killed mutation attempts fail closed, later observations supersede stale unknown state, retry evidence stays scoped to the exact workflow attempt, and the existing repair command remains the only GitHub mutation authority.

target.title: feat(dashboard): chart review handoff pressure
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a compact **Review handoff pressure** panel to OpenClaw Bay. It shows whether the exact-review admission queue is rising, falling, or steady over the last three hours, with the current waiting count and stepped pending/leased lines.

## Problem

The operational overview exposes the current exact-review handoff queue, but Bay only showed the animated work snapshot. That made it hard to see whether admission pressure was building or clearing while using the visual view.

## Implementation

- Stores queue-owned snapshots in the existing exact-review Durable Object when the queue changes: five-minute buckets, three-hour retention, at most 37 points.
- Replaces a point inside the current bucket instead of growing the history on each mutation.
- Keeps pressure telemetry explicitly best-effort: a history read/write failure cannot interrupt queue admission, claims, completion, or dispatch.
- Renders a responsive Bay panel with a plain-language direction, current pending count, coral pending line, and dashed teal leased line.
- Extends the deployment smoke contract and regenerates the deterministic Bay browser proof bundle.

## API footprint

This change adds **no GitHub REST or GraphQL calls** and no browser-side GitHub requests. The history is small Durable Object storage local to the existing exact-review queue and is recorded on queue mutations, not on Bay page refreshes.

Bay still consumes the shared `/api/status` response on its existing 20-second browser refresh. The API footprint is therefore unchanged at GitHub, but this PR does not claim a measured end-to-end API advantage over the Overview page.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build:dashboard`
- `node --test test/dashboard-worker.test.ts test/dashboard-smoke.test.ts` — 110 passing
- `pnpm run lint:dashboard`
- `git diff --check`
- Deterministic Chromium proof on Crabbox local-container: `cbx_e42103e2f43c` (`coral-barnacle`), 28 assertions; zero browser GitHub API requests and zero mutation requests. The regenerated storyboard, trace, and JSON summary are included under `docs/proof/openclaw-bay/`.
- `codex review --uncommitted` — clean after accepting and fixing the telemetry-failure and stale-proof findings.
- `codex review --base origin/main` — clean; no actionable correctness findings.

## Risks and rollout

- There is intentionally no historic backfill: a newly deployed queue starts with “Collecting queue history” and develops a trend as queue mutations occur.
- The chart is operational telemetry, not a scheduling control; queue mutations remain correct even if history storage is temporarily unavailable.
- `#555` is related current-pressure telemetry work; this PR is intentionally independent and only adds the bounded historical series and Bay presentation.

## User-facing note

OpenClaw Bay now makes the review handoff backlog trend visible without making the visual demo poll GitHub more aggressively.
